headline: Bank of Korea Keeps Base Rate Unchanged at 3.00%
summary: The Monetary Policy Board of the Bank of Korea decided to leave the Base Rate unchanged at 3.00% during its intermeeting period.
why: The Bank of Korea is the central bank of South Korea, responsible for formulating monetary policy and maintaining price stability. Changes to the base rate directly influence borrowing costs and economic activity nationwide.

impacts.name: South Korea
impacts.why: Maintaining the base rate at 3.00% leaves domestic borrowing costs unchanged, impacting consumer loans and corporate financing conditions.

why_moved: Leaving the base rate unchanged at 3.00% matched prior market expectations of a pause, limiting immediate volatility in South Korean won assets.
